title: Predicting Malignant Nodules from Screening CT Scans

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Predicting Malignant Nodules from Screening CT Scans》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Objectives · abstract-1-1】The aim of this study was to determine whether quantitative analyses ("radiomics") of low-dose computed tomography lung cancer screening images at baseline can predict subsequent emergence of cancer.

evidence.text: The aim of this study was to determine whether quantitative analyses ("radiomics") of low-dose computed tomography lung cancer screening images at baseline can predict subsequent emergence of cancer.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Predicting Malignant Nodules from Screening CT Scans》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Methods · abstract-2-1】Public data from the National Lung Screening Trial (ACRIN 6684) were assembled into two cohorts of 104 and 92 patients with screen-detected lung cancer and then matched with cohorts of 208 and 196 screening subjects with benign pulmonary nodules. Image features were extracted from each nodule and used to predict the subsequent emergence of cancer.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Predicting Malignant Nodules from Screening CT Scans》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Results · abstract-3-1】The best models used 23 stable features in a random forests classifier and could predict nodules that would become cancerous 1 and 2 years hence with accuracies of 80% (area under the curve 0.83) and 79% (area under the curve 0.75), respectively. Radiomics outperformed the Lung Imaging Reporting and Data System and volume-only approaches. The performance of the McWilliams risk assessment model was commensurate.

【Conclusions · abstract-4-1】The radiomics of lung cancer screening computed tomography scans at baseline can be used to assess risk for development of cancer.
